title: a-bulk-move-forwards-itself-from-gits-own-rename-record
intention: When the corpus moves in bulk, the forwarding that keeps every berthed packet's addresses resolvable is DERIVED from git's own rename record instead of authored one address at a time on a ticket.
why:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 by shaking the whole nest over the census. 307 findings stand across the corpus, and 306 of them are ONE CAUSE wearing three sieve names:

  survey_holdings_resolve   188 findings over 6 components
  constraint_traces          94 findings over 6 components
  charted_refs_resolve       24 findings over 7 components
  proofs_exist                1 finding  (unrelated — builder)

Behind those 306 findings are 130 DISTINCT addresses and 378 occurrences, and every one of them is a berthed packet naming a file at the layout the corpus had before the rung move (cairn/<name>/ -> cairn/{tools,machines,devices}/<name>/) and the chart dissolution (chart/ -> skills/chart/). Not one is a claim that was false when it was written. Each was true at berth time and the ground moved under it.

THE LIVED SYMPTOM, and it is not the count: build_inspector is the promotion gate. 306 standing findings mean that today, a component cannot be promoted without a reader hand-sorting real drift out of reorg residue — and the reader who does that sorting under time pressure is the reader who learns to skim the whole class. That is how a gate stops gating: not by being switched off, but by being right about so many things that nobody reads it. The gate's own founding failure was 'done' reported while the files stood unmoved (2026-07-24); a gate drowned in reorg residue cannot catch the next one.

AND THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY WRONG-SHAPED. `_forwarding_map` reads a `forwarding` order off the TICKET: `{from: {to, why}}`, authored by hand, checked at both ends. That shape is right for a deliberate single move a build makes on purpose. Aimed at a bulk reorg it asks a hand to type ~465 entries that git already recorded as it happened — and a hand-typed forwarding table is a second, hand-maintained copy of a fact the repository holds authoritatively. Law 1: re-deriving a settled answer is a defect, and this one is settled in the object store.

falsifier.proves_green: (1) DERIVE, DO NOT AUTHOR: the forwarding a bulk move needs is computed from `git log --diff-filter=R -M -C`, transitively followed, and confirmed against the file existing on disk NOW — a rename record whose target is gone forwards nothing. (2) A DIRECTORY IS A CONSENSUS OVER ITS FILES, not a new source: derived from the tracked files that were under it, and stated as such where a reader can see it. (3) THE HAND-AUTHORED ORDER SURVIVES AND KEEPS PRECEDENCE. `_forwarding_map` is right for a deliberate move a build makes on purpose, and it is the only thing that can speak for a DISSOLUTION (cairn/chart/intention+why.json went into skills/chart/, and no rename records that). Derivation fills the bulk; the ticket still says the things git cannot know. (4) THE DERIVATION IS MEASURED, NOT ASSERTED: whatever ships reports how many addresses it resolved and how many it did not, because the residue is the part a hand must then answer for.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when a shake of the nest over the whole census reports the reorg residue as ZERO without any hand-authored entry for a moved-not-dissolved address, AND the two genuine dissolutions are named on a ticket by a hand. WRONG INTENT if: (1) the sieves are narrowed to stop reading old packets before Akien has ruled the invariant — that is answering his question by shipping; (2) the derivation is cached into a checked-in table, which recreates the hand-maintained second copy under a machine's name; (3) an address is forwarded to a target that does not exist on disk, which forwards a live reader into a hole — worse than the red it replaced; (4) the residue count is suppressed rather than reported, because the residue is precisely the set a hand still owes.
falsifier.horizon: The derivation is one build and it is small — the measurement above IS the prototype, and it ran in one pass over the repo. The disposition of the 306 is NOT one build and is not startable until the invariant is ruled.
